quoted: When a receiving communication device does not support the superimposition of two or more characters at the same position [GR18, cite.py OK]; each message or message segment will begin on the next available character position of the communication device [GR2, OK]; If vertical positioning is not applicable on the device, the MCS will ignore the vertical positioning specified or implied [GR12, OK]; it is possible to present two or more characters at the same position [GR16, OK]; does not support the replacement of characters [GR17, OK]
reason: I could not write the witness. The one literal opening, that a GR2 device also 'does not support superimposition' so GR18's antecedent holds and segments 2..n of one message land on 'the same line' (DDD|EEEEE|FF -> literal GR18 'FFEEE'), proves too much. A variable-length device supports neither superimposition nor replacement, so on that reading GR17 (superimpose) and GR18 (replace) would both apply to the same SEND with contradictory results, and both would contradict GR2's placement at 'the next available character position'. The consistent reading is that GR16-GR18 classify the character-imaging, line-oriented devices of GR16, onto whose used line a SEND is positioned by vertical positioning (ADVANCING 0 LINES, REPLACING LINE). The code matches the premise: every device (a destination with no deliverTo, a terminal) is written only by McsStore.Transmit, which writes the concatenated segments of each complete message plus a newline at the committed end (RandomAccess.Write(handle, text, end)), and never at an occupied position. ADVANCING and REPLACING never reach it (GR12). The only bytes overwritten are a dead or refused statement's uncommitted tail past the committed end, and those were never transmitted (the statement took no action), so they are not 'characters previously transmitted'. Pre-existing file bytes with no line end are followed by the next message at the next position, which is again GR2. The set of WiseOwl devices to which GR18 applies is empty.

quoted: does not support the replacement of characters [GR17, OK]; it is possible to present two or more characters at the same position [GR16, OK]; each message or message segment will begin on the next available character position of the communication device [GR2, OK]; If vertical positioning is not applicable on the device, the MCS will ignore the vertical positioning specified or implied [GR12, OK]
reason: Judged the proposed DRV-1985-GR-XIV.3.6.4-17 (unpopulatable-antecedent; the set of GR16-class devices, of which GR17's device is a case, is empty). I could not write a GR17 witness. A GR17 witness needs a SEND whose characters land on a used line from its leftmost position. The only ways to put a SEND on a used line are vertical positioning (ADVANCING 0 LINES, REPLACING LINE), which every WiseOwl device ignores under GR12, and the segments or portions of one message, which GR2 places at 'the next available character position', not at the leftmost one. Reading GR17 literally on a variable-length device runs into the same contradiction as GR18: such a device supports neither replacement nor superimposition, so GR17 and GR18 would both apply with opposite results. The premise is true of the code. Devices are the terminals and the destinations with no deliverTo (MessageDefinitions.Devices). McsStore.Transmit is their only writer, and it writes the concatenated segments of each complete message plus a newline at the committed end. The new probe tried the last route left, a portion with indicator 0 plus ADVANCING 0 LINES REPLACING LINE onto a used line. It was placed contiguously (GR2) and nothing was superimposed. Consequence for the row: the current CONFORMS notes ('so no earlier characters share its line') are false and its test (1985-GR-XIV_3_6_4-17.cob, expected output 'SENT') never reads the device. The proposed derivation should replace that verdict and its notes, not sit beside them.
